note.en: New floor: GMI Cloud now lists GB200 on-demand at $8.00/GPU-hr, marked 'AVAILABLE NOW' on GMI's own pricing page (confirmed today) — the first sub-$10 on-demand GB200 rate seen, undercutting CoreWeave's long-standing $10.50/GPU-hr listing (still live, $42/hr for a 4-GPU instance). Oracle Cloud bare-metal remains the best-corroborated mid-point at ~$16.00/GPU-hr, which pulls the reasoned median down to ~$13.25/GPU-hr (midpoint of the two confirmed on-demand configs) from last cycle's Oracle-anchored $16.00 read. Azure's ND GB200 v6 bare-metal is unchanged at $108.16/hr for a 4-GPU ND128isr node (re-confirmed today) = $27.04/GPU-hr, still the ceiling. AWS's 1-year reserved rate of $10.58/GPU-hr is unchanged, still the only published contract figure for this SKU.

sources.label: Spare Cores — Azure ND128isr NDR GB200 v6 pricing

note.en: Floor moves slightly: DeepInfra's $3.69/GPU-hr on-demand listing (confirmed today, 'no wait times, no complex configs') edges out Packet.ai's $3.75/GPU-hr Dynamic-tier rate as the cheapest confirmed on-demand price. Note Verda's headline $3.12/GPU-hr is a spot rate, not on-demand — Verda's own on-demand price is $6.23/GPU-hr, so it's excluded from the floor. Typical price holds near ~$6.01/GPU-hr, consistent with today's cross-provider read (CoreWeave $4.26-$8.60, Nebius $3.95-$7.15, Civo $3.79-$4.49, Oracle $14.00). Ceiling unchanged: Google Cloud's a4-highgpu-8g still prices at $16.11/GPU-hr (re-confirmed today), above Oracle's bare-metal $14.00/GPU-hr. Still no clean published 1-year rate.

Reclassified the floor: Vultr's own preemptible-instances announcement and Spheron's pricing breakdown both confirm today that Vultr's ~$2.59/GPU-hr rate is a preemptible/spot SKU, not on-demand ('preemptible instances give customers... even lower cost' than Vultr's own on-demand line) — so it no longer qualifies as the on-demand floor. True on-demand pricing clusters at OVHcloud/Vultr on-demand ~$7.10/GPU-hr and CoreWeave ~$7.20/GPU-hr, with Oracle bare-metal still the ceiling at $8.60/GPU-hr (the only rate Spheron calls 'verified true on-demand'). CoreWeave's $4.25/GPU-hr 1-year reservation remains the only published contract rate for this SKU. Coverage is still thin (4 tracked providers); watch for a first-party Vultr on-demand rate card to pin this down further.

sources.label: Vultr blog — AMD Instinct GPU preemptible instances

note.en: Min from FluidStack ($2.30/GPU-hr, re-confirmed on their own pricing page today). Typical price drifted back up to ~$4.40/GPU-hr (GetDeploying's tracked median as of Sept 6, flat over the trailing 90 days) from last cycle's $4.30 read, as cheap capacity (GMI Cloud $2.60, Jarvislabs $3.99 on-demand/$1.99 spot) is offset by mid-tier providers (Hyperbolic, Crusoe, DigitalOcean, Nebius) clustering $4.0-4.6. Hyperscaler ceiling unchanged: Azure's ND96isr H200 v5 still prices at $110.24/hr for 8 GPUs = $13.78/GPU-hr — no reserved SKU exists for that instance. Reserved-rate listings still average ~$3.72/GPU-hr.

sources.label: Vantage — Azure ND96isr H200 v5 instance pricing

note.en: Floor drops: Lium.io's H100 80GB HBM3 pool is confirmed live today with 27 GPUs in stock at $1.30-$2.75/GPU-hr, and GetDeploying's verified-in-stock tracker separately flags Lium at ~$1.55/GPU-hr (Sept 9 read) — both below the prior Vast.ai floor of $1.73/GPU-hr, so the floor moves to Lium's $1.30. Typical price eased slightly to ~$3.29/GPU-hr (down from $3.39) as this cheaper Lium/Verda/Latitude.sh/Gcore/Cudo Compute cluster ($1.3-1.8/GPU-hr, all re-confirmed today) broadens the low end, while budget PCIe capacity (Vultr ~$2.99, Hyperbolic ~$3.19, Thunder Compute ~$3.20, re-confirmed) still clusters just below the median. Hyperscaler ceiling unchanged via Vantage at Azure's ND96isr H100 v5, $98.32/hr ÷ 8 GPUs = $12.29/GPU-hr (re-confirmed today), still above AWS (~$6.88) and Google Cloud (~$10.98) list prices. Per SemiAnalysis, 1-year contract rates were around $2.35/GPU-hr as of spring 2026 (not reconfirmed this cycle).

sources.label: Vantage — Azure ND96isr H100 v5 instance pricing

note.en: Aggressively priced for its 192GB of HBM3: TensorWave still anchors the low end at ~$1.71/GPU-hr (re-confirmed today, still a sales-quote rate with no self-serve checkout), while Azure's ND96isr MI300X v5 list price re-confirmed on cloudprice.net today spans $48-96/hr across regions ($6.00-$12.00/GPU-hr), ceiling unchanged. Typical pricing eased further to ~$2.79/GPU-hr (Thunder Compute's tracked median across 6 configs, down from $2.92 last cycle), with a wider low-cost cluster now tracked — Vultr (~$1.85), Hot Aisle (~$1.99), Runpod/GPU Outlet (~$2.39), DigitalOcean (~$2.59), all re-confirmed today — pulling the center down from the hyperscaler premium. DigitalOcean's 12-month reserved rate holds at $1.91/GPU-hr.

Legacy workhorse in steady decline: floor holds at Vast.ai's marketplace ~$0.53/GPU-hr (confirmed range $0.39-0.67 depending on host reliability; Vast.ai's own headline listings quote lower still for SXM4/PCIe variants at low-reliability hosts, not used here), well below Thunder Compute's own $1.09/GPU-hr anchor. GetDeploying's tracked median eased to ~$1.69/GPU-hr (flat over the trailing 90 days per their Sept 9 read, though ~7% above a year ago) from last cycle's $1.76-1.80 range, with GCP a2-ultragpu still listing ~$5.07/GPU-hr at the top. Civo's tiered 80GB rate card is unaffected — $1.79 on-demand, $1.59 at 12 months, down to $1.39 at 36 months; most other contract demand has moved to H100/H200.

sources.label: Civo — NVIDIA A100 GPU cloud pricing

note.en: Floor moves back: Lium.io's L40S pool is confirmed live and in stock again today (14 pods, 38 GPUs available) at $0.38-$0.75/GPU-hr, so the floor returns to $0.38/GPU-hr, undercutting GPU Outlet's $0.47/GPU-hr. Typical pricing holds at ~$1.53/GPU-hr — GetDeploying's tracked median is independently re-confirmed today at the same level (up ~19% since August 2025), so last cycle's jump was not a fluke; Runpod (~$0.79), gpu.ai/Vast.ai (~$0.80) and CoreWeave (~$0.99) still cluster below it. Ceiling holds near $3.5-3.8/GPU-hr (AWS us-east-1 8x config at $3.77; Oracle bare-metal at $3.50). Civo's rate card is unchanged and re-confirmed: $1.29 on-demand, $0.89 at 36 months.

sources.label: Civo — NVIDIA L40S GPU cloud pricing

note.en: Consumer flagship on marketplaces only (no hyperscaler offering): Salad Cloud still floors the market at ~$0.25/GPU-hr, unchanged since launch and re-confirmed today. Ceiling unchanged: Beam's serverless rate ($1.09/GPU-hr, re-confirmed on Beam's own pricing page) remains the priciest widely-published on-demand option — Beam's own on-demand (non-serverless) tier now lists from ~$0.72/GPU-hr, well below its serverless ceiling. Median eased further to ~$0.54/GPU-hr (AIMultiple's tracked median, down from $0.59 last cycle) as cheap marketplace capacity keeps expanding.

Vast.ai's marketplace floor is holding near ~$0.13-0.14/GPU-hr — marketplace pricing is volatile and hour-to-hour reads vary. Serverless-billed providers keep the ceiling near $1.61/GPU-hr (Beam, re-confirmed by AIMultiple); trackers that exclude serverless configs read a lower ~$0.74-0.77 top, so the ceiling carries over pending a closer look. Typical pricing has eased slightly to ~$0.42/GPU-hr — down about 13% over the trailing 90 days per a fresh GetDeploying-based read (Sept 2), continuing a slow downward drift as Theta EdgeCloud, GPU.ai and Novita add cheap capacity. Novita's 12-month reserved rate of $0.27/GPU-hr remains the only contract figure tracked for this SKU.
